# Gcore Edge Cloud

> Gcore Cloud offers on-demand IaaS and PaaS with compute, storage, networking, containers, databases, and observability across 30+ regions.

- [Cloud](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud.md): Gcore Cloud offers on-demand IaaS and PaaS with compute, storage, networking, containers, databases, and observability across 30+ regions.
- [Bandwidth and traffic](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/bandwidth-and-traffic.md): Bandwidth limits and traffic billing for Gcore compute resources, including VMs and Bare Metal servers.
- [Billing](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/billing.md): Gcore Edge Cloud uses pay-as-you-go billing with per-minute charges, a 4 EUR or USD threshold, and suspension if payment fails.
- [Tags](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/tags.md): Tags are key-value pairs for organizing and identifying Gcore Cloud resources, with rules, filtering, and cost report usage.

## Getting started
- [Manage resource quotas](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/getting-started/request-a-quota-increase.md): Check Gcore Cloud account quotas by region and request resource limit increases for compute, storage, network, and other services.

## Projects
- [Create and manage projects](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/getting-started/projects/create-a-project.md): Create and manage Gcore Cloud projects to organize isolated resources, control access, edit details, and delete projects.

## Users
- [User roles and rights](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/getting-started/projects/users/user-roles-and-rights.md): Compare the Client Administrator, Project Administrator, Project User, and Project Observer roles and the permissions each one grants.
- [Add users to a project](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/getting-started/projects/users/add-a-new-user-to-your-project.md): Invite new or existing users to a Gcore project by email, assigning a role such as Client Administrator or Project Administrator.
- [Manage user access](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/getting-started/projects/users/manage-user-access-to-your-project.md): Manage user access to a cloud project by editing roles, denying access, and restoring permissions for project members.
- [View user actions](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/getting-started/projects/users/view-user-actions.md): Track Cloud resource management operations with filters for resource name, project, date range, region, action type, and resource type.
- [Cost reports](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/getting-started/view-statistics-on-expenses.md): View Cloud cost reports and reservation cost reports to track resource usage, commitments, and export cost data.

## Virtual Machines
- [Types of Virtual Machines](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/virtual-instances/types-of-virtual-machines.md): Compare Gcore Virtual Machine types including Standard, GPU, CPU, Memory, High-frequency, Basic, TPM, and Network optimised.
- [Create a virtual instance](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/virtual-instances/create-an-instance.md): Create Linux or Windows virtual instances in Gcore Cloud by selecting region, image, VM type, volumes, networking, and authentication.
- [Customize the initial setup for a Virtual Machine](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/virtual-instances/customize-initial-setup-for-your-instance.md): Configure a Virtual Machine initial setup with cloud-init user data for passwords, users, SSH keys, and first boot scripts.
- [Check the operational status of a Virtual Machine](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/virtual-instances/check-the-operational-status-of-your-instance.md): Check the operational status of a Virtual Machine, including status, vm_state, and task_state values for instances in a project.
- [Enable root user on a Linux VM](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/virtual-instances/enable-root-user-on-a-linux-vm.md): Enable root user on a Linux VM with temporary sudo commands or permanent cloud-init configuration changes.

## Connect
- [Connect to a Virtual Machine via the Gcore customer portal](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/virtual-instances/connect/connect-to-your-instance-via-control-panel.md): Connect to a Gcore Virtual Machine using the browser-based VNC console for Windows and Linux troubleshooting.

## Connect via SSH
- [Connect to a Virtual Machine via SSH](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/virtual-instances/connect/connect-via-ssh.md): Connect to a Gcore Virtual Machine over SSH using key pairs or a password, with security group rules and PuTTY key conversion steps.
- [Configure and manage SSH keys](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/virtual-instances/connect/connect-to-your-instance-via-ssh.md): Generate, add, and manage SSH keys for Linux Virtual Instances, including deleting keys and stopping key sharing.
- [Convert an SSH key to PPK format](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/ssh-keys/convert-an-ssh-key-from-pem-to-ppk.md): Convert an OpenSSH SSH key to PPK format for PuTTY using PuTTYgen.
- [Establish SSH connection to a Virtual Instance](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/virtual-instances/connect/establish-ssh-connection-to-an-instance.md): Connect to a Linux Virtual Instance over SSH using a key pair, OpenSSH, PuTTY, Terminal, Command Prompt, or WSL.

## Placement groups
- [About placement groups](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/virtual-instances/placement-groups/about-placement-groups.md): Gcore placement groups define how Virtual Machines share or spread across physical servers with affinity and anti-affinity policies.
- [Configure a placement group](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/virtual-instances/placement-groups/configure-a-placement-group.md): Create and manage placement groups to control how Virtual Machines are distributed across physical hosts with affinity policies.

## Volumes
- [Volumes](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/virtual-instances/volumes/about-volumes.md): Gcore cloud block storage volumes for Virtual Machines, covering boot and regular volumes and volume types like High IOPS SSD and Standard.
- [Create and configure a volume](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/virtual-instances/volumes/create-and-configure-volumes.md): Create, configure, attach, resize, snapshot, and delete Gcore volumes for Virtual Machines.
- [Monitor load and performance of a Virtual Machine](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/virtual-instances/monitor-load-and-performance-of-your-instance.md): Monitor Virtual Machine load and performance with CPU, RAM, network, and disk metrics in Gcore.

## Snapshots
- [Take a snapshot of your file system](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/virtual-instances/snapshots/take-a-snapshot-of-your-file-system.md): Create and manage Gcore volume snapshots for system and regular volumes, including restoring and building virtual machines.
- [Set up automatic snapshot creation](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/virtual-instances/snapshots/set-up-automatic-snapshot-creation.md): Set up automatic snapshot creation schedules for cloud volumes, including creating, disabling, enabling, and deleting schedules.

## Troubleshooting
- [Troubleshoot issues with an SSH connection](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/virtual-instances/troubleshooting/troubleshoot-issues-with-ssh-connection.md): Fix SSH connection failures on Gcore virtual machines and bare metal servers, including key, username, public IP, and firewall problems.
- [Recover SSH access in recovery mode](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/virtual-instances/troubleshooting/recover-ssh-access-via-recovery-mode.md): Recover SSH access in recovery mode by installing a public key on a Linux VM or Bare Metal server when the private key is lost.

## Bare Metal servers
- [About Bare Metal](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/bare-metal-servers/about-bare-metal-servers.md): Gcore Bare Metal is a cloud service offering dedicated physical servers with full isolation and high performance.
- [Types of Bare Metal servers](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/bare-metal-servers/types-of-bare-metal-servers.md): Compare Gcore Bare Metal server types for high frequency, infrastructure, and storage workloads.
- [Create a Bare Metal server](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/bare-metal-servers/create-a-bare-metal-server.md): Create a Gcore Bare Metal server by selecting a region, image, server type, and network interfaces, then requesting a quota increase.
- [Manage a Bare Metal server](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/bare-metal-servers/manage-a-bare-metal-server.md): Manage a Bare Metal server with console access, power controls, network interfaces, tags, rebuild, rename, and delete operations.
- [Connect to Bare Metal via SSH](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/bare-metal-servers/connect-to-your-bare-metal-server-via-ssh.md): Connect to a Linux Bare Metal server via SSH using key pairs or a password, with steps for Windows, Linux, and macOS.
- [Bare Metal egress traffic](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/bare-metal-servers/egress-traffic.md): Bare Metal egress traffic is billed per GB over the public network interface, while private network traffic stays free.

## Troubleshooting
- [Troubleshoot issues with an SSH connection](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/virtual-instances/troubleshooting/troubleshoot-issues-with-ssh-connection.md): Fix SSH connection failures on Gcore virtual machines and bare metal servers, including key, username, public IP, and firewall problems.

## Advanced DDoS protection
- [About advanced DDoS protection for Bare Metal](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/bare-metal-servers/advanced-ddos-protection/about-advanced-ddos-protection-for-bare-metal-servers.md): Advanced DDoS Protection for Bare Metal filters attack traffic through TMS, keeps servers online, and offers always-on mitigation.
- [Activate advanced DDoS protection for Bare Metal](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/bare-metal-servers/advanced-ddos-protection/activate-advanced-ddos-protection-for-bare-metal-servers.md): Activate Advanced DDoS Protection for Bare Metal servers during creation or on existing public interfaces and manage profiles.

## Images
- [About images](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/images/about-images.md): An image is a copy of a disk file system used to create a virtual machine boot volume or distribute software.
- [Upload a custom image](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/images/upload-an-image-to-the-storage.md): Upload a custom image to Gcore from a public URL after checking supported formats, drivers, packages, and start modes.
- [Manage custom images](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/images/manage-custom-images.md): Manage Gcore Cloud custom images by viewing, renaming, tagging, deleting, and creating virtual instances from them.

## Networking
- [Create and manage a network](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/networking/create-and-manage-a-network.md): Create and manage Gcore Cloud networks, attach or detach network interfaces to VMs, Bare Metal, Load Balancers, and Kubernetes clusters.
- [Create and manage a subnet](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/networking/create-and-manage-a-subnetwork.md): Create and manage a subnet in a Gcore cloud network, including CIDR, DHCP, DNS, router settings, renaming, and deletion.
- [Create and manage a router](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/networking/create-and-manage-a-router.md): Create and manage a Cloud Router in Gcore, attach subnets, configure static routes, and control traffic between networks.

## IP address
- [Create and configure a floating IP address](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/networking/ip-address/create-and-configure-a-floating-ip-address.md): Create, configure, reserve, assign, detach, and delete a floating IP address for Gcore Virtual Machines and Bare Metal servers.
- [Create and configure a reserved IP address](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/networking/ip-address/create-and-configure-a-reserved-ip-address.md): Create, assign, detach, and delete Gcore reserved IP addresses for virtual machines, bare metal servers, and load balancers.
- [Create and configure a virtual IP address](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/networking/ip-address/create-and-configure-a-virtual-ip-vip-address.md): Create and configure a virtual IP address (VIP) in Gcore Cloud for failover with Keepalived or as a secondary address.
- [Difference between virtual, floating, and reserved IP addresses](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/networking/ip-address/difference-between-virtual-floating-and-reserved-ip-addresses.md): Compare virtual, floating, and reserved IP addresses in Gcore Cloud, including use cases, assignment, failover, and billing.
- [Configure an allowed address pair](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/networking/ip-address/configure-an-allowed-address-pair.md): Configure allowed address pairs on a private network port to permit extra IP or CIDR addresses for a virtual machine.

## Load balancers
- [Create and configure a load balancer](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/networking/create-and-configure-a-load-balancer.md): Create and configure a Gcore load balancer with region, flavor, network, listeners, pool, health check, timeouts, logging, and tags.
- [Add TLS certificates to a load balancer](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/networking/load-balancers/add-certificates-to-load-balancer.md): Add TLS certificates to a load balancer listener using SNI and Secrets Manager for multiple secure domains.
- [Configure mutual TLS authentication](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/networking/load-balancers/configure-mtls-authentication.md): Configure mutual TLS authentication for Gcore Load Balancers with server and CA certificates, TLS termination, and backend mTLS.
- [Manage load balancers](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/networking/load-balancers/manage-load-balancers.md): Manage Gcore load balancers, including statuses, settings, listeners, monitoring, logging, tags, DDoS protection, limits, and failover.
- [Logging for load balancers](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/networking/load-balancers/logging-for-load-balancers.md): Enable load balancer logging to send access logs to Gcore Logging, configure namespaces, topics, and destination regions.
- [Use annotations for load balancers](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/networking/load-balancers/use-annotations-for-load-balancers.md): Configure Gcore Load Balancers in Managed Kubernetes with annotations for type, flavor, IP, listeners, pools, logging, and DDoS protection.
- [Monitoring for load balancers](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/networking/load-balancers/monitoring-for-load-balancers.md): Monitor load balancers with a Prometheus metrics listener and Managed Logging that sends access logs to OpenSearch.
- [Add and configure a security group](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/networking/add-and-configure-a-firewall.md): Create and manage security groups for Virtual Machines, including rules, tags, default groups, and Bare Metal servers.
- [Bring Your Own IP (BYOIP)](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/networking/byoip.md): Bring Your Own IP (BYOIP) lets organizations use their own public IP ranges with Gcore while preserving IP reputation and allowlists.
- [Cloud egress IP addresses](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/networking/cloud-egress-ip-addresses.md): Find Gcore Cloud egress IP addresses and ranges to allowlist outbound traffic and automate allowlist updates.

## File shares
- [About file shares](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/file-shares/about-file-shares.md): Gcore File Shares provides NFS file storage for sharing data across Virtual Machines, Bare Metal servers, and Kubernetes pods.
- [Configuring file shares](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/file-shares/configure-file-shares.md): Create and resize Standard NFS and VAST file shares for Linux VMs, Bare Metal servers, and GPU clusters.
- [Resize file shares for Managed Kubernetes](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/file-shares/resize-file-shares-for-kubernetes.md): Resize Standard NFS file shares for Managed Kubernetes by scaling workloads to zero, expanding the share, then remounting.
- [Migrate data from S3 and EFS to Gcore](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/file-shares/how-to-migrate-data-from-s3.md): Move data from Amazon S3 or EFS to Gcore Object Storage or File Shares using rclone for cloud storage migration.

## Managed Kubernetes
- [About Gcore Managed Kubernetes](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/kubernetes/about-gcore-kubernetes.md): Gcore Managed Kubernetes runs container workloads on Gcore Cloud with bare metal nodes, autoscaling, autohealing, and a 99.99 percent SLA.
- [Bare Metal Kubernetes](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/kubernetes/bare-metal-kubernetes.md): Deploy Kubernetes worker nodes directly on Bare Metal servers for dedicated hardware, high performance, and isolation.

## Clusters
- [Create a Kubernetes cluster](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/kubernetes/clusters/create-a-kubernetes-cluster.md): Create a Managed Kubernetes cluster in Gcore with worker pools, networking, autoscaling, and kubeconfig access.
- [Upgrade a Kubernetes cluster](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/kubernetes/clusters/upgrade.md): Upgrade a Managed Kubernetes cluster to a newer version with rolling worker node replacement and version checks.

## Connect
- [Connect to your nodes via SSH](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/kubernetes/clusters/connect/connect-to-your-nodes-via-ssh-using-a-floating-ip-address.md): Attach a floating IP address to a Kubernetes worker node and allow inbound SSH to connect using the cluster SSH key.
- [Install kubectl and connect to a Kubernetes cluster](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/kubernetes/clusters/connect/install-kubectl-and-connect-to-a-kubernetes-cluster.md): Install kubectl and connect to a Kubernetes cluster on Windows, Ubuntu, Linux, macOS, including kubeconfig setup and certificate renewal.
- [Secure Kubernetes cluster with OpenID Connect](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/kubernetes/clusters/secure-cluster-with-oidc.md): Enable, update, or disable OpenID Connect authentication to secure Kubernetes clusters with centralized single sign-on access control.

## Autoscaling
- [About autoscaling](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/kubernetes/clusters/autoscaling/about-autoscaling.md): Autoscaling adjusts node count in a Managed Kubernetes pool based on load, keeping it between the minimum and maximum.
- [Change autoscaling limits](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/kubernetes/clusters/autoscaling/change-autoscaling-limits.md): Adjust the minimum and maximum node counts for a Managed Kubernetes node pool to match expected workload changes.
- [Create and configure a pool](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/kubernetes/clusters/autoscaling/create-a-new-pool-in-cluster.md): Create and configure a Kubernetes node pool with autoscaling, placement, taints, labels, autohealing, kubelet, container runtime settings.
- [Advanced cluster autoscaler settings](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/kubernetes/clusters/autoscaling/advanced-cluster-autoscaler-settings.md): Configure advanced cluster autoscaler settings, including cluster expander and parameters for scan interval and scale-down decisions.
- [Configure GPU autoscaling for Kubernetes](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/kubernetes/clusters/autoscaling/configure-gpu-autoscaling-for-kubernetes.md): Set up GPU autoscaling for Kubernetes with NVIDIA GPU Operator, KEDA, Prometheus, and Gcore Cluster Autoscaler.
- [Add users with limited rights to a Kubernetes cluster](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/kubernetes/clusters/add-users-with-limited-rights-to-a-kubernetes-cluster.md): Create a namespace-scoped ServiceAccount and kubeconfig to give limited Kubernetes cluster access without admin credentials.
- [Monitor load on a specific node](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/kubernetes/monitor-load-on-a-specific-node.md): View CPU, RAM, network traffic, and packet metrics for a Kubernetes worker node in Gcore Managed Kubernetes.

## Networking
- [About networking in Kubernetes](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/kubernetes/networking/about-networking-in-kubernetes.md): Kubernetes networking routes external traffic to application pods using Services, Ingress, and Ingress Controllers.
- [Install nginx Ingress controller](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/kubernetes/networking/install-and-set-up-the-nginx-ingress-controller.md): Install and set up the nginx Ingress Controller on Kubernetes with Helm, then get the Load Balancer IP address.
- [Use Nginx Ingress Controller](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/kubernetes/networking/use-the-nginx-ingress-controller.md): Create an Ingress object with the nginx Ingress Controller to route incoming requests to a Service using routing rules and a manifest.

## Storage
- [Create a PVC and bind to a pod](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/kubernetes/storage/create-a-pvc-and-bind-it-to-a-pod.md): Create a Kubernetes PersistentVolumeClaim, bind it to a pod, and resize it using Gcore Managed Kubernetes persistent storage.
- [Configure NFS storage for Managed Kubernetes](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/kubernetes/storage/configure-nfs-csi-driver-for-kubernetes.md): Set up NFS storage for Managed Kubernetes by creating a File Share that maps to a StorageClass for persistent volumes.
- [Troubleshooting a node in a "Not Ready" state](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/kubernetes/troubleshooting-not-ready-state.md): Diagnose and fix a Kubernetes node stuck in Not Ready state by checking node conditions, capacity, Kubelet logs, and errors.

## Managed PostgreSQL
- [About managed PostgreSQL](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/managed-database-postgresql.md): Gcore Managed PostgreSQL is a fully managed cloud database with automatic maintenance, high availability, and PostgreSQL 13 to 15 support.
- [Manage a PostgreSQL server](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/managed-database-postgresql/manage-postgresql-servers.md): Create, configure, connect to, upgrade, and delete a Gcore Managed PostgreSQL server, including credentials and psql or pgAdmin access.
- [Backup and restore PostgreSQL database for Managed PostgreSQL using external utilities](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/managed-database-postgresql/backup-and-restore-postgresql-database-for-gcore-managed-database-for-postgresql-using-external-utilities.md): Back up and restore Gcore Managed PostgreSQL databases with pg_dump and pg_restore external utilities.

## Secrets manager
- [Configure secrets for HTTPS load balancer](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/secrets-manager/upload-a-pkcs12-file.md): Configure SSL TLS secrets for HTTPS load balancers by uploading a PKCS12 file or adding certificate fields directly.

## Function as a service
- [About Function as a Service](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/faas/about-function-as-a-service.md): Gcore Function as a Service runs code on demand without managing servers, scaling automatically from zero and charging only for execution.
- [Authenticate to functions with API keys](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/faas/authenticate-to-functions-with-api-keys.md): Create, edit, and delete access keys to protect function endpoints and authenticate requests with a key header.
- [Code examples for supported FaaS runtimes](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/faas/code-examples-for-supported-faas-runtimes.md): Code examples for FaaS runtimes include basic functions, dependency handling, and request access for .NET, Go, Java, Node.js, and Python.

## Container as a service
- [About container as a service](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/caas.md): Gcore Container as a Service runs containers in the cloud without Kubernetes or virtual machine management.
- [Create a container](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/caas/create-a-container.md): Create and run a containerized application in Gcore Cloud with image, port, flavor, autoscaling, and logging settings.
- [Use a private container registry](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/caas/use-a-private-registry.md): Deploy a container from a private image by creating registry credentials and a pull secret for Gcore Container as a Service.
- [Build and deploy containers to CaaS via GitHub Actions](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/caas/build-and-deploy-containers-to-caas-via-github-actions.md): Build and deploy containers to Gcore Container as a Service using GitHub Actions workflows.
- [Manage containers](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/caas/manage-containers.md): Manage Gcore containers by checking statuses, updating settings, viewing logs, and starting, stopping, or deleting containers.

## Container registry
- [Container registry](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/container-registry.md): Container Registry stores Docker images and OCI artifacts for Gcore products, with free storage and per-user push and pull permissions.
- [Create a Container Registry](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/container-registry/create-container-registry.md): Create a Gcore Container Registry, add a user, and push or pull OCI-compatible images and artifacts.
- [Manage container registries](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/container-registry/manage-container-registries.md): Manage container registry storage limits, images, artifacts, users, permissions, and registry deletion in Gcore.

## Managed logging
- [About managed logging](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/logging-as-a-service/about-logging-as-a-service.md): Managed Logging collects and stores logs from virtual machines and bare metal servers, with access through OpenSearch Dashboards.
- [Configure logging and view logs](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/logging-as-a-service/configure-logging-and-view-your-logs.md): Set up Gcore Managed Logging to collect infrastructure logs, deliver them to Kafka topics, and search them in OpenSearch Dashboards.

## Install a log shipper
- [Install and configure Filebeat](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/logging-as-a-service/install-a-log-shipper/install-and-configure-filebeat.md): Install and configure Filebeat to ship logs to Gcore Managed Logging for viewing in OpenSearch Dashboards.
- [Install and configure Fluent Bit](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/logging-as-a-service/install-a-log-shipper/install-and-configure-fluent-bit.md): Install and configure Fluent Bit to collect logs and send them to Gcore Managed Logging for OpenSearch Dashboards.
- [Install and configure Fluentd](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/logging-as-a-service/install-a-log-shipper/install-and-configure-fluentd.md): Install and configure Fluentd with the Kafka output plugin to send logs to Gcore Managed Logging.
- [Install and configure Logstash](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/logging-as-a-service/install-a-log-shipper/install-and-configure-logstash.md): Install and configure Logstash to send logs to Gcore Managed Logging using Kafka output and the Kafka Integration Plugin.
- [Prometheus exporter](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/logging-as-a-service/prometheus-exporter.md): Configure the Prometheus exporter to expose OpenSearch index metrics and review key metric definitions.
- [View Gcore Managed Logging data in Grafana with OpenSearch plugin](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/logging-as-a-service/view-opensearch-logs-in-Grafana.md): Connect Gcore Managed Logging to Grafana using the OpenSearch plugin to view and visualize logs.

## Terraform
- [Manage Cloud resources via Terraform v0](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/manage-cloud-via-terraform.md): Manage Gcore Cloud resources such as Virtual Machines, networks, and volumes using the v0 provider and configuration files.
- [Manage Cloud resources via Terraform v2](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/manage-cloud-via-terraform-v2.md): Manage Gcore Cloud infrastructure as code with provider v2, covering SSH keys, security groups, networks, volumes, and virtual machines.
- [Manage cloud resources via Ansible](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/manage-cloud-via-ansible.md): Manage Gcore Cloud resources with Ansible by installing the Galaxy collection and running playbooks.

## Use cases
- [Set up a mailing server in a Gcore Cloud VM](https://docs.gcore.com/cloud/use-cases/set-up-a-mailing-server-in-gcore-cloud-vm.md): Set up a mail server on a Gcore Cloud VM with Postfix and Dovecot on Ubuntu or Debian, including port 25 unblocking.
